question.text:
A processor has 5 stages: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, and Writeback. The latencies of each stage are given below:
\begin{array}{|l|l|l|}
\hline Stage & Latency & \\
\hline Fetch & 300 ps & \\
\hline Decode & 400 ps & \\
\hline Execute & 350 ps & \\
\hline Memory & 550 ps & \\
\hline Writeback & 100 ps & \\
\hline
\end{array}

In the pipelined version, assume each pipeline register adds an overhead of 20 ps .
What is the cycle time, latency of one instruction, and maximum throughput of the pipelined processor?

  1. Cycle time $=550 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=2750 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 550 ps
     
  2. Cycle time $=570 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=2850 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 570 ps
     
  3. Cycle time $=570 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=1700 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 570 ps
     
  4. Cycle time $=550 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=1700 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 550 ps

question.text:
A non-pipelined processor has the following stage latencies:
\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline Stage & Latency \\
\hline Fetch & 300 ps \\
\hline Decode & 400 ps \\
\hline Execute & 350 ps \\
\hline Memory & 550 ps \\
\hline Writeback & 100 ps \\
\hline
\end{array}

Assume no overhead between stages in the non-pipelined design.
Which of the following is correct regarding the non-pipelined processor?

  1. Cycle time $=550$ ps, Latency $=1700$ ps, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 550 ps
     
  2. Cycle time $=400 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=2000 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 400 ps
     
  3. Cycle time $=1700 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=1700 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 1700 ps
     
  4. Cycle time $=1700 \mathrm{ps}$, Latency $=550 \mathrm{ps}$, Throughput $=1$ instruction every 1700 ps

question.text:
A program consists of 500 instructions in total, including a loop of 100 instructions that is executed 25 times. Initially, all instructions are stored in main memory, and the cache is empty.
Assume:

  • Main memory access takes 10 units of time
  • Cache access takes 1 unit of time
  • The cache is large enough to hold all loop instructions
  • Program execution time depends only on the time taken to fetch instructions (operand data access is ignored)

What is the speedup achieved by using the cache?
Provide your answer as a numerical value rounded to 2 decimal places.
